name: Colofn Cymry
text: Colofn Cymry is Welsh for the pillar of Wales or Cambria. The phrase is an epithet of Caradog, the ancient British chieftain whom Roman writers called Caractacus. MacKillop records the Welsh praise-title under its own headword and points to the hero's entry. See Caradog.

attributes.attribute: Welsh epithet meaning the pillar of Wales

okr.objective: Colofn Cymry is the Welsh pillar-of-Wales epithet of Caradog.
key_results: The name translates as the pillar of Wales or Cambria.
MacKillop attaches the epithet to Caradog, Rome's Caractacus.
